environment_freeze.built_ins: restricted to Read,Grep,Glob,Bash via --tools on every run
environment_freeze.mcp: --strict-mcp-config on every run; C0 uses {"mcpServers":{}}, C2 uses treesitter_query only
environment_freeze.no_agent_or_subagent_tools: Task/Agent explicitly in --disallowedTools on every run
environment_freeze.no_edit_write_todowrite: Edit,Write,TodoWrite explicitly in --disallowedTools on every run
environment_freeze.no_websearch_webfetch: WebSearch,WebFetch explicitly in --disallowedTools on every run
environment_freeze.no_claude_md_or_rtk: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1 plus --setting-sources project,local (excludes user-level CLAUDE.md/RTK hook config)
environment_freeze.fresh_session_per_run: --no-session-persistence, new run directory per official run, no --resume/--continue
environment_freeze.prompt_as_first_message: the committed prompt file's full text is passed as the -p argument itself, so it is necessarily the first and only conversational user message

harness_smoke_test.goal: Determine whether Claude Code 2.1.70 can execute a fresh read-only tool-using session non-interactively via -p under --permission-mode default when the exact required tools are explicitly preapproved, without any bypass flag.
harness_smoke_test.method: tools/benchmark_c4/run_condition.py invoked directly (not via the official run_all_c4.ps1 path) against a disposable, non-benchmark smoke directory and, for one probe, the real C4 worktree read-only.

runs.verdict: PASS -- default permission mode with --allowedTools does not hang or prompt interactively

runs.purpose: denial-boundary: --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash (no Write), asked the model to try Write anyway
runs.result: exit=0, wall_s=7.23, result="WRITE_RESULT=UNAVAILABLE", file not created, permission_denials=[]
runs.verdict: PASS -- --tools genuinely removes Write from the surface (tool unavailable, not merely denied-with-prompt); nothing broader than the named read-only tools was silently granted

runs.purpose: MCP-shaped: --strict-mcp-config with treesitter_mcp_config.json (treesitter_query only), --allowedTools includes mcp__treesitter_query__treesitter_query, real C4 worktree as cwd (read-only ask)
runs.result: exit=0, wall_s=11.02, result="TREESITTER_RESULT=godot/assets/marble_machine/course/course_modules.gd:264-278:method:_apron_y" (matches verified ground truth exactly), permission_denials=[]
runs.verdict: PASS -- the provider tool launches under --strict-mcp-config, is callable under default permission mode via --allowedTools, and returns genuinely relevant, correct output; no bypass flag was used

harness_smoke_test.conclusion: --allowedTools under --permission-mode default (a) preapproves exactly the named tools, (b) does not broaden the available tool surface beyond --tools' restriction, (c) leaves --strict-mcp-config's MCP isolation intact, and (d) requires no bypassPermissions/dangerously-skip-permissions. Validated and frozen before any official run, per Phase 7's condition for using this harness.

nested_session_safety.mechanism: tools/engineering_runner/redaction.child_environment(), an existing reviewed allowlist utility already used by tools/benchmark_c2 and tools/benchmark_c3 for the same purpose: forwarding only a small named-variable allowlist (plus PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8) to the child process so the orchestrating (this) session's own credentials, session markers, and nested-session detection do not leak into or confuse the spawned official-run session.
